Colony care

A colony needs no daily fuss: once a week top up the water, put out food and clear the leftovers. Below is what each species needs and what you do it with. Buy a colony together with a formicarium and the food and tool kit come free.

What to feed

Diet depends on the species: harvesters need seeds, the rest need live protein. All of them need sugar syrup, two or three times a week.

  • Messor StructorSeeds and grains
    Seed mix for harvester antsFeeder beetle culture
  • Formica CuniculariaSugar syrup, insects
    Feeder beetle culture
  • Formica RufibarbisInsects, sugar syrup
    Feeder beetle culture
  • Lasius NeglectusSugar syrup, insects
    Feeder beetle culture
  • Lasius NigerSugar syrup, insects
    Feeder beetle culture
  • Camponotus FellahProtein and sugar syrup
    Feeder beetle culture

Seed mix for harvester ants

A mix of small seeds the harvesters turn into «ant bread». One container lasts a Messor colony 4-5 years.

80 лей

Feeder beetle culture

A live-food culture that breeds itself. You buy it once.

150 лей

What to tend it with

Tweezers pull out leftovers, the syringe and pipette deliver water, the brush sweeps ants off the lid without crushing them. Wash in warm water without detergent - ants are sensitive to smells.

Formicarium tool kit

Ten small things that turn colony care from a struggle into a routine.

150 лей

Worth remembering

Humidity
A colony survives a week without food, but not dried-out brood. Top up the water when the chambers lighten. Keep the arena dry - especially for harvesters, or the grain moulds.
Rehousing
No rush: a young colony stays in its tube until the workers get cramped - usually 20-30 of them. Do not move them by hand: darken the new nest, leave the old one lit, and the colony walks over on its own.
Leftovers
Remove live food and syrup the next day. If you do not, mould and flies take hold in the arena, and clearing them out is far harder than preventing them.
